items.title: Breaking: Coalition reunion expected to be announced after last-minute deal
items.description: A breakthrough deal to reunite the Coalition is expected to be announced today after 11th-hour talks between the leaders of the Liberal and National parties.

items.title: Liberals craft permission structure to oust Sussan Ley
items.description: A permission structure has been crafted for Liberals to ditch the first woman to lead the federal party room before she has even had a year in the role.

items.title: Daytime power prices have never been lower. So why are bills rising?
items.description: The benefits of extremely low energy prices during the day are "washed away" by extremely high ones after dark. But there is light at the end of the tunnel.

items.title: Dodgy doctors who targeted NDIS clients are shifting to veterans
items.description: Fraudsters taking advantage of people with disability now appear to be targeting veterans, prompting a $200 million crackdown by the federal government.

items.title: Stakes enormous as Australia considers DNA screening for newborns
items.description: From rare cancers caught early to dementia foretold decades in advance, newborn genomic testing raises an unsettling question: Just because we can know, should we?

items.title: Before Steve Irwin, there was Alby Mangels. This is why you no longer hear his name
items.description: In the 1980s, Alby Mangels was a box office star. The filmmaker wowed Australian audiences with his exotic adventures, but at the height of his fame he disappeared. In a rare interview he reveals what went wrong.

items.title: As West wakes up to the Epstein class, China plans global reserve currency
items.description: As the West reacts to the revelations in the latest batch of Epstein files, China has plans for the renminbi to become a global reserve currency.

items.title: Cyclone Mitchell threat not over after wild night in WA's Pilbara
items.description: Karratha residents will assess damage from the category three cyclone as it continues to track along the Pilbara coast.

items.title: Olympic quick hits: Skier wears tank top, Carey lip-syncing drama emerges
items.description: A Finnish skier makes a questionable fashion choice on the slopes, while Mariah Carey faces claims she was lip-syncing at the opening ceremony. Here are the quick hits from the Winter Olympics.

items.title: After the uprising, Bangladesh returns to the ballot with its wounds still open
items.description: Bangladesh is heading back to the ballot box in what is being billed as its first free and fair election in more than a decade.

items.title: An Australian travel CEO crash-landed this week. Some saw an accident long ago
items.description: Australian travel mogul Jamie Pherous, who grew a three-man operation into a multi-billion dollar success, foundered on the rocks of an accounting scandal in the UK.

items.title: Then and now: Walking the Overland Track with my father
items.description: Ron Preuss first walked the 65-kilometre-long Overland Track in 1987. Now, he returns decades later with his daughter Maren to see what has changed.

items.title: One of Sydney's biggest parties got axed. Why did it happen?
items.description: This is what we know about why one of the biggest LGBTQIA+ celebrations has been called "disastrously organised".

items.title: 'Mixed feelings' about a viral trend embracing Chinese culture
items.description: Some Chinese Australians have mixed feelings about the sudden global embrace of Chinese culture after the trend emerged late last year.

items.title: You'll do badly, but don't let that stop you from trying this week's Hard Quiz
items.description: I'm honestly surprised you're back. I genuinely didn't expect to see you so soon after last week's dismal effort.

items.title: Seasonal fruit and veggie choices that can help you save this month
items.description: From grapes to red capsicum, here's how to prioritise some of this season's best fruit and veg.

items.title: From campfire songs to a stadium‑size solo show: Xavier Rudd levels up
items.description: Xavier Rudd performs solo these days, but he carries a spirit with him wherever he goes.

items.title: The story of opal queen Isabel Gray blurs the lines of myth and legend
items.description: The infamous Isabel Gray was known by many names and fronted court for sly grogging and stood accused of running a brothel.

items.title: 'We saved our lives': How a Canberra-based refugee fled Venezuela
items.description: Josh Madrid was arrested for attending a pro-democracy protest in Venezuela. 24 hours later, he fled his homeland, fearing he would be killed by the government.

items.title: Almost half a billion dollars paid to victims of crime over three years in Qld
items.description: The ABC can reveal the state government has paid almost $500 million to tens of thousands of victims of crime over the past three financial years.

items.title: Illegal e-bikes to be seized and destroyed in major NSW crackdown
items.description: Devices found to be going over the state's e-bike speed limit will be seized and destroyed by authorities, under expanded police powers.

items.title: Tasmania explores homebirths, AMA says focus should be making hospitals comfortable
items.description: The Tasmanian government is developing a public homebirth model that would allow midwives working in the public system to support women to labour from their homes.

items.title: After 30 years, has the time finally come for a national gun register?
items.description: First proposed after the Port Arthur massacre in 1996, Australia still doesn't have a national gun register. As Queensland parliament sits for the first time since national gun reforms became law, advocates say it is time to centralise firearm information.

items.title: Americans propose an end to Russian-Ukrainian war by June, Zelenskyy says
items.description: America has given Russia and Ukraine a June deadline to end the war — and will put pressure on both sides to ensure it is met — Volodymyr Zelenskyy says.

items.title: 'Teflon president' may be no more as Trump does the unthinkable
items.description: Donald Trump has, until now, thrived in controversy. But the US president has now done something that a year ago would have been unthinkable: deleted a social media post.
